title.narrative: The overall objective of the project is to promote new technology in order to improve energy efficiency and modernise the distribution grid of Dhaka city based partially on digitalisation.

description.narrative: For shaping the future, AFD pushes this last dimension with national utilities in transmission and in distribution sectors in many countries; and specifically in Bangladesh. The modernisation of the grid based on classical solutions using data as Digital Control System, can be deployed and even accelerated by using digital substations in the different nodes of the grid. Other additional bricks such as: smart meters, electrical vehicle, virtual power plan will strengthen the trajectory to a smarter grid. Even more, the different Renewables should become Dispatchable Power units which can cover partially the primary energy demand thanks to the flexibility brought by the digital solutions, and the competitive cost of this type of generation. Flexibility is a crucial element of this scenario.

title.narrative: The specific objectives of the Smart Grid Pilot project are: to develop a small scale smart grid network on pilot basis consisting of five 33/11 KV substations with a view to demonstrate and realise the benefit of smart grid implementation, to strengthen DPDC through institutional and technical capacity development for operation and maintenance of smart grid network, to disseminate the lessons learnt from this pilot and perform costbenefit analysis to gradually scale up smart grid for rest of DPDCs distribution network.

description.narrative: This pilot smart grid system is aimed at building a strategy for the coming years regarding adaptation to recent technological advancement in power sector. The success of the project will encourage DPDC to scale up the system for its remaining network. Lessons learnt from this pilot will enable other power distribution utilities in Bangladesh to gradually implement smart grid. However, the main challenges of the pilot will be to develop a good communication network and skill the labour force so that sustainability of the output can be achieved.The present smart grid project is fully relevant with power and energy development strategy described in the Power System Master Plan, which is a key pillar of the 7th Five Year Plan 2016 2021. The strategy specifically includes a rapid growth in electricity generation, the improvement of power sector efficiency, and the reduction of transmission and distribution losses.The energy sector for the growth of the country is a major target taken in account by the Vision 2021, which schedules electricity for all by 2021.

title.narrative: The specific objectives of the Smart Grid Pilot project are: to develop a small scale smart grid network on pilot basis consisting of five 33/11 KV substations with a view to demonstrate and realise the benefit of smart grid implementation, to strengthen DPDC through institutional and technical capacity development for operation and maintenance of smart grid network, to disseminate the lessons learnt from this pilot and perform costbenefit analysis to gradually scale up smart grid for rest of DPDCs distribution network.

description.narrative: This pilot smart grid system is aimed at building a strategy for the coming years regarding adaptation to recent technological advancement in power sector. The success of the project will encourage DPDC to scale up the system for its remaining network. Lessons learnt from this pilot will enable other power distribution utilities in Bangladesh to gradually implement smart grid. However, the main challenges of the pilot will be to develop a good communication network and skill the labour force so that sustainability of the output can be achieved.The present smart grid project is fully relevant with power and energy development strategy described in the Power System Master Plan, which is a key pillar of the 7th Five Year Plan 2016 2021. The strategy specifically includes a rapid growth in electricity generation, the improvement of power sector efficiency, and the reduction of transmission and distribution losses.The energy sector for the growth of the country is a major target taken in account by the Vision 2021, which schedules electricity for all by 2021.
